acceptanceCriteria: The ordering the test needs (foreign reap before exit observation) is forced deterministically, e.g. by a hook or barrier, rather than by timing
The test still fails on a reintroduced V1-1055 regression (a group operation after the concurrent release), shown by an injected mutation
-count=50 under synthetic CPU contention on Linux passes, numbers retained
body: Observed in release-gates nightly run 38559681509 job 115837380133 (ubuntu-24.04, full-gate, schedule, head 8803b7ddc5d1c4c91affc4102e684cc432bad439, Go 1.27.2, 2026-10-14 11:58:57Z): internal/procgroup process_posix_test.go:295 'the foreign reap never preceded the exit observation', test 4.63s; the only failing package in that job. Expected: the test arranges a foreign reap before the owner's exit observation deterministically, or reports the ordering it could not force as a skip with reason. Actual: the ordering race lost on the hosted runner. Suspected test-ordering flake under hosted scheduling, not a confirmed product defect; distinct from V1-1368 (descendantSnapshotTimeout), V1-1374 (escaped child reap under -race) and V1-1244 (/proc thread count). Earlier nightlies 10-09..10-13 failed on other tests. Blocks a green release-gates nightly for 1.0.0-rc.3. Raw log retained in the orchestrator scratch nightly/115837380133.log.
title: procgroup TestV11055NoGroupOperationAfterConcurrentRelease fails on hosted ubuntu-24.04: the foreign reap never preceded the exit observation
